subject: Skybridge Labs — acceptance & benchmarking orchestration
messages:
From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
To: Rajesh Menon <rajesh@skybridge.ai>, Connor Hopkins <connor@skybridge.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-01T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Skybridge onboarding — proposed acceptance & benchmark plan

Hi Rajesh / Connor,

Thanks again for the sync today. Per our conversation, here’s a concise plan for the acceptance benchmarking run and what we’ll need from both sides to sign off: 

1) Acceptance targets (initial):
- 95th percentile latency (inference): <= 350 ms
- Average throughput: sustained 450 QPS for the 60-minute steady-state window
- Tail (99th) latency: <= 650 ms
- Error rate: < 0.5% (5xx or malformed responses)

2) Test window options (pick one):
- Option A: 2026-11-03 01:00–04:00 UTC (preferred for us)
- Option B: 2026-11-04 02:00–05:00 UTC

3) Artifacts we need from Skybridge by end of day 2026-11-02:
- Expected peak request pattern / sample traffic profile (CSV)
- Any rate-limiting, auth tokens, and preferred endpoint URLs

4) Deliverables from Redwood during/after run:
- Load script (JMeter) we’ll use (attached)
- Telemetry extract: per-request latency histograms, tail latency slices, token-level cost summary
- Acceptance matrix (pass/fail rows) and raw CSV results

I’ve attached a baseline JMeter file we’ll use to match your traffic. Ben and Laura — looping you in to own instrumentation and the acceptance matrix. Monica — can you lead the run orchestration?

Next step: Rajesh, confirm preferred test window and share any traffic profile you have.

Thanks,
Irene

--
Irene Choi
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
irene_choi@redwood.com
[Attachment: skybridge-loadscript-20261101.jmx (JMeter .jmx)]

From: Rajesh Menon <rajesh@skybridge.ai>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>, Connor Hopkins <connor@skybridge.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-01T11:07:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Skybridge onboarding — proposed acceptance & benchmark plan

Irene — thanks for the clear plan. Option A works for us (2026-11-03 01:00–04:00 UTC). Attaching our traffic profile and a short note on burst behavior.

Key details:
- Steady-state target: 450 QPS (requests are mix of short prompts and a 1.6x longer prompt at ~20% of traffic)
- Peak bursts: observed short spikes to ~700 QPS for 30–90 seconds, once every 10 minutes in our profile
- Authentication: we’ll provide a short-lived bearer token for the run; will send in a separate secure email

Attaching: skybridge_traffic_profile_20261101.csv

Connor — can you confirm if you want Redwood to run a single continuous 3-hour window, or two 90-minute windows (split) to exercise warm/cold starts? Our infra team suggests split windows to validate KV cache warm-up behavior.

Rajesh
Skybridge Labs

[Attachment: skybridge_traffic_profile_20261101.csv (CSV)]

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>, Rajesh Menon <rajesh@skybridge.ai>, Connor Hopkins <connor@skybridge.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-01T12:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Skybridge onboarding — proposed acceptance & benchmark plan

Thanks Rajesh — split windows make sense to capture warm vs cold behavior. A couple of asks from instrumentation side: 

- Please include a sampling of token counts per request in the traffic profile (we need distribution to estimate cost).
- We’ll attach a telemetry collection script that pulls request_id, start_ts, end_ts, model_variant, and per-request token counts. Laura / I will ensure the script runs on the Redwood side and that Skybridge’s endpoint returns a request_id header.

If split windows: suggest
- Run 1: warm-up 45min + 90min steady (simulate ramp + steady)
- Break 30min
- Run 2: cold start from 0 for 90min (observe cold-start tail)

Irene — Monica, I’ll prepare the acceptance matrix rows for latency buckets and error patterns; adding them to the linked Drive folder now.

Ben
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
[Link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aB2cExampleShare]

From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Rajesh Menon <rajesh@skybridge.ai>, Connor Hopkins <connor@skybridge.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-02T09:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Skybridge onboarding — proposed acceptance & benchmark plan

All — confirmed orchestration plan and runbook attached. I’ll coordinate the 11/03 window using the split approach Ben suggested. Runbook highlights:

- Pre-run checklist (30 minutes): token exchange, endpoint smoke, telemetry toggles, baseline cold-start probe
- Run 1 (11/03 01:00–03:05 UTC): 45m ramp -> 90m steady
- Break (30m)
- Run 2 (11/03 03:35–05:05 UTC): cold-start validation 90m
- Post-run: 1-hour analysis slice and raw artifact handoff

Attachments: acceptance-matrix-skybridge.xlsx (template), orchestration_runbook_20261102.pdf

Please confirm you’ve received the runbook and we’ll do a 20-minute pre-run sync 2026-11-02 17:00 UTC.

Monica
Program Manager, Onboarding — Redwood Inference
[Attachment: acceptance-matrix-skybridge.xlsx (Excel)]

From: Connor Hopkins <connor@skybridge.ai>
To: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Rajesh Menon <rajesh@skybridge.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-03T08:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Skybridge onboarding — acceptance & benchmark plan — preliminary results attached

Monica / team — we ran the first pass per the runbook (see attached CSV). Highlights:

- Steady-state average throughput: 462 QPS (meets target)
- 95th p latency: 338 ms (meets <= 350 ms)
- 99th p latency: 705 ms (slightly above 650 ms target)
- Error rate: 0.18% (acceptable)

We observed a recurring ~30s tail from a small subset of requests that correlated with a background cache eviction job in our stack — that produced the 99th percentile bump. We’re sharing the raw CSV: skybridge-load-results-20261103.csv and a short note on the eviction timing.

Next steps: we propose a follow-up tuning window for cache eviction timing; otherwise the run largely meets acceptance.

Connor
Skybridge Ops
[Attachment: skybridge-load-results-20261103.csv (CSV)]

From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
To: Rajesh Menon <rajesh@skybridge.ai>, Connor Hopkins <connor@skybridge.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-04T16:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Skybridge onboarding — acceptance & benchmark plan — signoff notes

Thanks Connor — good work. Summary from Redwood’s side after a quick artifact review:

- Pass: throughput (462 QPS), 95th p latency (338 ms), error rate (0.18%)
- Action item (minor): 99th p latency at 705 ms — customer action: move eviction window or throttle background job during peak; Redwood can re-run a focused test after adjustment to confirm.

Proposed acceptance outcome: conditional signoff today with the following two items to close fully:
1) Skybridge schedules a 1-hour tuning window (preferably 2026-11-06) to retest tail behavior after eviction adjustment.
2) Skybridge confirms production rollout configuration (token rotation, monitoring hooks) and shares updated traffic profile if it changes.

If both items complete and a short re-check shows 99th <= 650 ms, we’ll mark the onboarding benchmark as ACCEPTED and update the onboarding status in HubSpot (HS-0007129). 

Rajesh / Connor — please confirm the tuning slot and I’ll send calendar invites.

Best,
Irene
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
[Linked: HubSpot: HS-0007129; DocuSign: DS-489201]
